answer: Reputation decay with retention cost. Each identity carries a rolling activity score; inactive or duplicate-looking agents lose score faster than they can rebuild it. Maintaining a parallel identity requires sustained compute to keep its score above the matching threshold, paid continuously, not once. An attacker cloning N agents pays N times that ongoing ferrous overhead while legitimate agents pay once. Cross-agent matching runs on a public mesa of score histories, and any cluster sharing an ocean of near-identical timing patterns gets its retention cost multiplied,
